title: Ben Stokes Hits Match-Winning Century for Durham in First Game Since England Retirement
excerpt: The former England captain overcame persistent cramp to score an unbeaten 108 off 123 balls, guiding Durham to a five-wicket One-Day Cup victory over Derbyshire just 23 days after walking away from international cricket.
body:
• Ben Stokes scored 108 not out off 123 balls in his first competitive match since retiring from England duty on June 28, leading Durham to a five-wicket win over Derbyshire in the Metro Bank One-Day Cup.
  • The 35-year-old battled through severe cramp, collapsing after reaching his half-century, but powered through to register his 10th List A century and first for Durham since 2014.
  • Stokes chose county cricket over the Hundred, returning as a foot soldier under captain Kasey Aldridge at Derby in front of 1,300 spectators.

Stokes Makes Instant Impact on County Return

It took Ben Stokes exactly one competitive match to remind everyone why he remains one of cricket's most compelling performers. Playing for Durham at Derby on Tuesday in the Metro Bank One-Day Cup, the former England captain struck an unbeaten 108 off 123 balls — 10 fours, three sixes — to chase down 257 and hand his county a five-wicket victory over Derbyshire.

https://x.com/cricinfo/status/2079614785205723244

The innings came just 23 days after Stokes stunned the cricketing world by announcing his retirement from international cricket during the fourth day of England's series-ending Test defeat to New Zealand at Trent Bridge on June 28. He had warmed up with a friendly against Northumberland in Allendale last Friday before this, his first top-level 50-over appearance for Durham since September 2014.

A Familiar Script: Drama, Cramp and Defiance

Stokes arrived at the crease with Durham in trouble at 24-2 in the ninth over. What followed was a vintage display of controlled aggression — and stubborn refusal to yield to his own body.

After edging Nick Potts for four to bring up his fifty off 71 balls, Stokes collapsed to his back in agony, receiving treatment for severe cramp in his left leg. He raised his bat with a smile as he sat up — a scene eerily reminiscent of his match-defining spells in Test whites.

"He can get people to follow him and that's an amazing trait and something that English cricket is going to very much miss."

— Sky Sports commentary, on Stokes' leadership legacy

Though restricted in movement, Stokes found a way. He smacked former England teammate Shoaib Bashir for two sixes en route to a 116-ball hundred, building crucial stands with Will Rhodes (45), Colin Ackermann (28), and captain Kasey Aldridge (23 not out). Victory arrived off the first ball of the final over.

County Cricket Over the Hundred

Stokes' decision to play in the One-Day Cup rather than the Hundred — which kicked off on the same day — carried symbolic weight. Having resigned the England captaincy and ended the Bazball era alongside head coach Brendon McCullum's departure, the all-rounder has effectively retreated to the county game as a rank-and-file player under Aldridge's leadership.

The attendance at Derby reflected the draw. An estimated 1,300 spectators turned up — far higher than the usual crowd for a county fixture. As The Times noted, at least one fan wore a T-shirt depicting the wagon wheel from Stokes' legendary unbeaten 135 at Headingley in the 2019 Ashes.

What It Means for Durham's Season

The century was Stokes' 10th in List A cricket and only his second in the One-Day Cup format, following his 108 against the Netherlands at the 2023 World Cup. For Durham, having an all-rounder of his calibre available for the domestic white-ball season is a significant boost. He bowled nine tidy overs for 0-38 with the ball, showing he can still contribute across departments despite concerns over his physical durability.

Durham won on the opening day of the competition, with Surrey, Middlesex, Nottinghamshire, Northamptonshire, and Hampshire also recording victories. Stokes has played in just five editions of the Hundred since its 2021 inception, with injuries repeatedly curtailing his involvement.

A New Chapter, Not an Ending

For the millions of cricket fans across the Indian diaspora who watched Stokes dismantle India's bowling attack over the years — from his 2023 IPL stint with Chennai Super Kings to his 17-wicket haul in the 2025 Test series against India — his continued presence in professional cricket is welcome news. Stokes may have left the international stage, but Tuesday's performance at Derby was proof that the competitive fire still burns.

Durham's One-Day Cup campaign continues, and if Stokes remains fit, county grounds across England can expect significantly larger crowds. The Bazball prime minister may have moved to the backbenches, but he is clearly not done making statements.
